current.title: NASA Made Atoms Colder Than 1 Kelvin
current.hook: Nature just lost its record for cold, and it wasn't even close.
current.closing: Human-built extreme cold lets researchers study matter in conditions nature cannot provide nearby.
current.question: What can ultracold atoms reveal?

segments.say: Empty space is 2.7 kelvin, but the Boomerang Nebula is colder—the natural benchmark NASA's lab beat.
NASA chilled atoms ten billion times colder than the Boomerang Nebula, reaching a temperature nature cannot match.
The lab orbits 250 miles overhead, while its natural comparison is quadrillions of miles away—extreme cold brought close.

held_for: judge: Only the cold-atom chamber is a real picture of the story. The hook opens on a dish and 'room temperature', and the distance beat is a rocket with a 17-digit number pasted over it.

judge.one_line: Only the cold-atom chamber is a real picture of the story. The hook opens on a dish and 'room temperature', and the distance beat is a rocket with a 17-digit number pasted over it.
problems: The hook (hook@0.3 to seg0:end) cycles 1 K, then 293 K, then 2.7 K over a turning radio dish. It never shows the shock (atoms 10 billion times colder than nature), so the first two seconds read as room temperature.
seg0 and seg1 are the same dish scene for about 9 seconds, and the dish says nothing about temperature.
In seg2, Data stands beside the chamber with his hand on his chin. The lever next to him is never pulled, so he is decoration in the key beat.
In seg3, a rocket launching from a beach is not the Cold Atom Lab in orbit, and '29,400,000,000,000,000' is an unreadable-in-meaning digit string carrying the whole claim.
The closing (seg4) reuses the seg3 rocket frame behind a wall of text. There is no visual payoff.
fixes: Open the hook on the payoff frame of the atom chamber: a frozen cluster with one huge 'colder than nature' readout. Drop 293 K from the hook.
Replace the dish scenes with one shot where temperature is physical. For example, a thermometer or cold scale Data cranks down past empty space (2.7 K) and the nebula (1 K), plunging off the bottom.
Have Data pull the chamber lever in seg2 so the atoms condense because he does it.
Redraw seg3 as a distance shot: the ISS just overhead, then pull back toward a far-off nebula speck. Say 'quadrillions of miles' in words.
Give the closing its own finished picture, such as the glowing lab in orbit with Data aboard, instead of a reused launch frame.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is at most two short spoken sentences and 24 words: the beat's number, then what it MEANS (why it is surprising, what it caused, why the viewer should care), nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 18 words and it says why this matters to the viewer, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.

Each beat is part of a STORY, not a readout, simple enough for a distracted viewer: at most ONE number a beat, said with what it means (a change in words: 'it nearly doubled'). Name no group a viewer would not know ('the experts', not 'the OECD'); the WHO, NASA and the White House are fine.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is clickbait, never a scam: the most surprising TRUE fact in the story, 5-14 words, said the way a person tells a friend. It makes sense heard once. 'You' only when it is the viewer's own money, body or kids. No formula tags ('...and nobody told you', '...shocking everyone'), no quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), no hedge (might, may), no vague size ('astonishing'). Exaggerate nothing.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
